title: Open-source peer capability matrix and 3D evidence boundaries
mode: deeper/broader primary-source research and plan refinement
scope: Refresh open-source DWG/DXF peer operation and version boundaries
Reconcile modeler-carrier writer omissions with per-source no-loss evidence
Separate strict DXF parsing, recovery, ACIS payload inspection, and B-rep conversion
Refine existing PAR-07/S8 implementation readiness without increasing per-slice validation

sources.observation: The manual distinguishes stable, unstable, and unhandled class states and states that R2010-R2018 DWG writing still fails CRC/audit checks. Treat it as a pinned read-side/structural comparator for exact supported profiles, not a general modern DWG writer acceptance oracle.

The project documents AFL++ campaigns and saved crash/hang/leak regression replay. Borrow only the failure classification and minimized-regression pattern at an existing scheduled hardening checkpoint; no peer fuzz corpus was copied or run.

The reporter says ACadSharp 3.4.9 reads DWG 3DSOLID/REGION entities but its DXF writer silently omits them, including solid-only blocks; the reporter says LibreDWG's census confirmed the source objects. No source drawing is attached and the report is not an independent local reproduction.

The README labels the project 0.1.0-alpha.1/pre-alpha; reports decoded, skipped, and errored counts on a dated 19-file corpus; says entity records are boundary-checked; and says DWG writer output lacks automated external-CAD acceptance. Corpus expansion changed its aggregate percentage, so that percentage is not a stable support score.

The policy permits the ODA public specification, eligible public DWGs, self-generated fixtures, and high-level algorithm descriptions; it explicitly forbids consulting LibreDWG implementation code. Its public ODA-spec lineage means it is a distinct implementation, not an independent normative authority.
The tutorial distinguishes ordinary readfile use on trusted DXF from recover.readfile for flawed files. A recovered document is a different outcome from strict parser acceptance.
browse-acis inspects and exports raw SAT/SAB content. It is useful for payload framing, not proof of B-rep semantics.
The drawing add-on lists ACIS rendering as unsupported and says it has no 3D rendering engine. A successful DXF parse or rendering pass therefore cannot qualify solid geometry.
The project calls itself experimental, documents selected SAT/SAB/ASM profiles and geometry, retains unsupported records as raw data, and warns that parsing does not guarantee conversion to a shape.
The geometry support table is profile-limited and rejects unsupported geometry rather than silently replacing it with sampled surfaces or returning a partially successful solid.

The documented SAB/ASM versions have unequal native/synthetic coverage; history is retained opaquely and not fully validated. The library uses CadQuery/OpenCascade conversion, so it does not establish an independent kernel result from OCCT-based consumers.

localCrosswalk.observation: The local source has an explicit modeler-geometry DXF writer route and generated syntax/test owners. This research pass did not run those tests or qualify external reopen, independent shape semantics, or native consumer acceptance.

planImpact.implementationSummary: Refined existing PAR-07/S8 comparator admission and no-loss reporting. The plan now distinguishes source and output modeler identity/owner disposition, strict DXF parse from recovery, ACIS raw inspection from shape conversion, and source/parser/kernel/consumer lineage. No local defect, test, fixture, dependency, or support claim was added.
planImpact.nextImplementation: The SectionViewStyle group-1 identifier/arrow position slice was completed and validated later in this work session. Continue with the next already-listed local-ready PAR-138 slice; do not wait for peer builds or external qualification.

method.limitations: Peer documentation and issues are mutable, route-specific, and not local reproductions. dwg-rs coverage counts are self-reported on a small dated corpus. ACadSharp #1195 has no public customer drawing. cq-acis profile support and OCCT conversion do not establish general ACIS, DWG AcDs association, or independent-kernel support.

validation.planEdit: Added a peer capability matrix, cross-route modeler no-loss requirements, and fast-first PAR-07/S8 refinements.
